data.hypothesis: This isolates ambient azimuth direction generation: pairing the sine and cosine evaluation may reduce per-ray trig-call overhead without changing either random draw, the float azimuth, or the intended independent sampling distribution. The prior valid T3 variant measured 3.348743 s versus the baseline's 3.496109 s, but its cause and per-configuration performance are unknown; the catalog shows only one distinct T3 source program so far. No speedup or correctness result is claimed for this candidate.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as context when comparing an isolated direction-generation variant against the prior ambient-intersection experiment; the prior measurement has no per-configuration breakdown.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior ambient sphere-origin precomputation variant was valid and measured 3.348743 s versus the valid baseline at 3.496109 s, but those aggregate measurements alone do not establish the mechanism or guarantee a gain on each configuration.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure paired ambient sin/cos independently on every official configuration, including nsubsamples=3, before considering combinations.

data.notes: This candidate changes only paired azimuth trigonometry in ambient-ray generation. It retains the two random draws in their original order, all 64 ambient rays, intersection calculations and conditions, geometry, primary-ray traversal, and scheduling. GCC/Clang use a guarded compiler builtin; other compilers retain separate sinf/cosf calls. Correctness and repeated timings are pending the controller's official configurations, including nsubsamples=3.
transformations: Add a paired-sine/cosine helper for the ambient azimuth using a compiler builtin on GCC/Clang and separate standard-library calls as the fallback.
Replace only the ambient-ray cosf(phi)/sinf(phi) pair with the helper; leave random draws, ray count, intersection work, primary-ray logic, and scheduling unchanged.
